To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the landfill leache studied is constituted of 60% of low molecular weight compounds, 80% of which were identified as intermediate products or products of condensation.
the residual COD of landfill leachates after aerobic degradation process are constituted by a high molecular weight fraction of refractory compounds.
the residual COD in the landfill leachates are mainly constituted of compounds with molecular mass >10 kDa.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the residual organic matter in the landfill leachates and their fractions after the aerobic degradation process, which is a step forward to a better understanding of the behavior of the leachates and to develop more efficient treatment processes.
the identification of the residual compounds that constitute the residual COD of landfill leachates and the characterization of their biodegradability.

the characterization of the compounds that are responsible for the residual COD of leachate and the characterization of the low and high molecular fractions of leachate, before and after the aerobic treatment process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the aerobic degradation of landfill is not effective for the complete removal of COD from the leachate.
the residual organic compounds of the leachate studied are mainly constituted of SMP and that they are characterized by a high molecular weight.
the compounds identified in leachate and in the effluents of its degradation process are mainly aliphatic and aromatic compounds, with a high molecular weight and refractory nature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the aerobic degradation of landfill landfill leachate generates a large number of compounds with high molecular weight and refractory nature that are not biodegradable and can be responsible for the high residual COD of the leachate.
the landfill leaches are constituted by compounds with different molecular weight.
the residual COD of the landfill leachates is composed of a high molecular weight fraction that is refractory to aerobic biodegradation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the residual COD of landfill leachates is mainly composed by SMP, and the aerobic process of degradation of landfill leaches does not remove the refractory COD of the landfill leachates.

a large fraction of the COD in landfill leachate is constituted by compounds with molecular weight below 10 kDa and the majority of the residual COD corresponds to intermediate and products of condensations of affluent compounds and SMP.

the characterization of the low and high molecular fractions of landfill leachates can be a useful tool for understanding the behavior of the compounds that are responsible for the residual COD of the effluents.
